This definitely feels like a troll post, from the inflammatory language, lack of formatting, and incredible dog-whistles.

Moving on to your primary question, though, people engage with media for many reasons. Two major reasons are as 1) Escapism, and 2) Reflection

Escapism engagement utilizes movies as way to relax, forget about the difficulties in life, and be able to enjoy entertainment. There are great escapist-genre movies, which often are more comedic or action-adventure. Fantasy and wish fulfillment are often a core component of Escapist Cinema. 

Reflection engagement utilizes movies as a way to evaluate the world around them, to reflect on society, oneself, or philosophy. They can be great tools to process difficult topics, as film adds a layer of separation between the audience and the topic. I don't really want to **talk** about the existential fears of getting older, but I will absolutely watch a movie that explores these themes.

In both of these types of engagement, Escapism and Reflection, sexuality and its depiction can be beneficial. Just like joy, sadness, and fear, sexuality is a common component for most human experiences. I don't see why it should be excluded "just because it's sex". Can it be depicted in better ways and worse ways? Absolutely. 

Film, however, has been used as a way to explore the human experience. And sexuality, in all its flavors, both positive and negative, is a part of the human experience.

Eh.

Action scenes in movies are there to excite.

Horror scenes are there to intimidate.

By that token, sex scenes are there to entice.

  
If a movie was absolutely reduced to the barest essentials of the narrative, most of our films would hardly exceed 75 minutes... The fact of the matter is that we tell stories to evoke a certain effect, and that effect is partially dependent on what that story houses in terms of scenes that "strive for effect."
